head_commit.message:
feat(prompt-enhancement): pe-4 rules, compaction summary, measured timeouts (v1.8.14)

Rules (pe-4, prompt-only):
- "TBD" moves from default to fallback: facts already present in the material
  (file names, symbols, line numbers, error types, stack, early project
  conventions) must be stated, not blurred into "related file"/"some error".
- Length now scales with complexity (120-250 / 250-450 / up to 700) instead of
  a hard 420-char cap.
- No backticks (including inline) and no ** - the composer renders plain text.

Earlier history without reading jsonl: pi's compactionSummary already sits in
the conversation. It is now cleaned of the UI header and injected as a
"summary" role, so "the plan we agreed at the start" is no longer invisible to
the rewriter. Reading ~/.pi/agent/sessions/*.jsonl would add path-encoding
coupling, parentId branch reconstruction and half-written-tail tolerance for
the same payoff, so it stays out.

Timeouts from measurement: 5 samples P50 4.1s / P90 7.7s -> server 25s->30s,
client 30s->35s.

Verified on the same "这个怎么修" input: output now cites
Kotlin/Compose, ChatScreen.kt:1841 and the early "minimal intrusion" rule,
657 chars, no backticks, one genuinely-needed TBD. Server tests: 86 pass.

head_commit.message:
feat(prompt-enhancement): feed tool results and full history into the rewriter (v1.8.13)

"feels like a demo" was not a prompt-quality problem. Measured on a real
session with 230 messages: assistant 109, toolResult 119, user 1 - and the old
code filtered every toolResult out, right where "this error" and "the part you
just changed" actually live.

Three changes, no new architecture:

- Include MessageRole.TOOL: toolName + command + output (falls back to preview;
  errors get an explicit marker).
- Use olderMessages + messages so paged-in history is covered too.
- Drop the 400-char cap on assistant replies (it truncated the previous plan)
  and raise the budget from 8/6000 to 12/12000.

Deliberately not done: reading ~/.pi/agent/sessions/*.jsonl (the client already
has the data), token estimation, relevance ranking, and prompt-rule changes.

Verified end to end in 5.7s: a tool result containing "unresolved reference:
enhancementEnabled at ChatScreen.kt:1841" made the output cite all four facts
while still honouring "do not change code". Server tests: 85 pass.

head_commit.message:
fix(workspace): unify backslash and forward-slash project paths

The same directory showed up as two workspace rows because the two entry
points stored it differently: the app persisted what /api/cwd/browse returns
(D:\myscript\termius, platform separators), while sessions/pi-web report
projectRoot from git (D:/myscript/termius). Grouping keyed on the raw string,
so `termius` appeared twice and its sessions only counted for one row.

Align with how pi-web already does it: projectKey (separator-normalized,
trailing separator stripped, case-insensitive on win32) is the grouping
identity, projectRoot stays the display path. Nothing is rewritten to make
the two sides look equal.

- add WorkspacePaths (toSlashes/displayPath/identityKey/samePath) and
  groupWorkspaces(); group by identity key, display the newest session path
- Session.workspacePath routes through the normalizer, new workspaceKey
- custom workspaces are canonicalized on write and normalized on read, so
  legacy backslash entries still display, still merge, and are removed by key
- pin/alias/selection/archive grouping/project session filters/new-session
  cwd all compare by identity key, keeping legacy entries working
- WorkspacePathsTest covers the screenshot scenario plus case/trailing
  slash/UNC/POSIX boundaries

Bump to 1.8.12 (versionCode 118).

head_commit.message:
fix(prompt-enhancement): stop capability-probe jitter from cancelling in-flight requests (v1.8.11)

499 is our own "client already gone" code, and it was being produced by two
bugs rather than by the user:

- The capability probe collapsed every failure into null, so one ping timeout
  turned promptEnhancementTarget into null, which retriggered the LaunchedEffect
  that cancels the in-flight enhancement. The client then dropped the connection
  and the gateway answered 499. The probe is now three-state (supported /
  explicitly unsupported / could-not-reach) and only the first two change the
  entry point; the connection+model identity is also pinned to its last good
  value so jitter cannot cancel a request or make canApply reject the fill-in.
- The server timeout only fired an abort signal. Providers that ignore the
  signal (DNS, TCP handshake, upstream queueing) left the await hanging, so the
  client's 30s callTimeout won the race and it looked like 499 again. The
  server now returns TIMEOUT(504) on its own at timeoutMs + 500ms.

Also: map 499 to CANCELLED and handle it silently (leaving a session or
cancelling is not a failure), and report local socket timeouts as
"enhancement timed out" instead of a generic failure.

Tests: 84 pass (server). Verified: normal run 7.4s/200; after abandoning a
request mid-flight the same session retries successfully in 3.8s.
